item.title: Helm Chart Values
item.description:
The layer5-cloud chart installs the Layer5 Cloud server and, as subcharts from the Ory repository, Kratos and Hydra. The defaults below are those of chart version 0.2.0, which ships with Layer5 Cloud v1.0.278. Run helm show values layer5/layer5-cloud to print the defaults of the version you install. For the install procedure, see Deploy Layer5 Cloud.

How values reach the server 🔗

The chart writes env.* values into one ConfigMap and one Secret, and the server pod reads both as environment variables. Sensitive values go to the Secret. Any change to either rolls the server pods, because the pod template carries a checksum of both.

item.title: Deploy Layer5 Cloud
item.description:
This guide installs the layer5-cloud chart, which deploys the Layer5 Cloud server together with Kratos and Hydra. It assumes you have made the decisions in Plan a Deployment. The commands use the release name layer5-cloud in the namespace layer5-cloud.

Prerequisites 🔗

  • A Kubernetes cluster and Helm 3.
  • An ingress controller that supports WebSocket upgrades, and a TLS certificate for your hostname.
  • A PostgreSQL server you can create databases on.
  • An SMTP relay that satisfies the mail constraints, or the decision to run without mail.
  • The OAuth applications for Google and GitHub, if you offer social sign-in.

Install 🔗

1. Prepare the database 🔗

Create one role and three databases on your PostgreSQL server, then create the uuid-ossp extension in the meshery database. The server creates the schema itself.

item.title: Snapshot a Helm Chart
item.description:
The Kanvas Snapshot Helm plugin renders a Helm chart as a Kanvas design image from your terminal. Use it to see what a chart deploys before you install it, or to put a picture of a chart in a review, a ticket, or a README. It needs no repository, no cluster, and no Layer5 Cloud account.

You give the plugin the URL of a packaged chart. The plugin imports the chart as a design, starts a render, and then prints the image URL or emails you when the image is ready.

item.title: Kanvas Snapshot
item.description:
Kanvas Snapshot turns an infrastructure-as-code file into a picture of the design it describes. It runs as a GitHub workflow or as a Helm plugin, not in the Kanvas canvas, so reviewers see the shape of a change (which components exist and how they connect) without reading YAML or opening Kanvas.

A snapshot is standalone. It never connects to your cluster and never deploys anything. It reads the file you point it at, builds a design from it, and renders that design to an image.

item.title: Self-Hosted Deployments
item.description:
A self-hosted deployment runs the same Layer5 Cloud that Layer5 operates, on infrastructure you control. Your users sign in against your identity services, your organizations and designs live in your database, and Meshery Servers in your network connect to your deployment as their remote provider. Your data stays in your database.

Self-hosting is part of the Enterprise plan.

What you deploy 🔗

One Helm chart, layer5-cloud, installs the identity-aware application and its two identity services. You supply the database, the ingress, and the TLS certificate.
